newsitem.title: USA: Anesta submits drug application to FDA.
newsitem.headline: Anesta submits drug application to FDA.

text.p: Anesta Corp said on Wednesday that it had submitted a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for Actiq (oral transmucosal fentanyl citrate) to treat "breakthrough" pain in chronic cancer pain patients.

The company said the new drug application was the first to include a breakthrough pain indication, and if approved, Actiq would be the first, and to this point only, product specifically cleared for this indication.
Abbott Laboratories' Hospital Products Division manufactures and intends to market Actiq under licence from Anesta in the United States, the company said.
Breakthrough pain occurs when transitory episodes of moderate to severe pain "break through" a baseline of otherwise controlled, persistent pain.
According to Anesta, it is reported in more than 50 percent of cancer pain patients in the United States.
